newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei bolts higher, chased by bulls in NY.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei bolts higher, chased by bulls in NY.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market resumed trade on Tuesday after a long weekend and bolted more than two percent higher in the morning session.
"The bulls on Wall Street are chasing the Nikkei average higher today," said Kenzo Doi, an analyst at Kokusai Securities.
Overnight, Dow Industrials soared to a record close for a second successive session, surging 51 points to about 5,889.
By Tokyo's midday close, the key Nikkei 225 was 350.39 points or 1.68 percent higher at 21,193.03 after earlier hitting 21,264.37.
The market was closed on Monday for a national holiday.
Doi said market sentiment had improved drastically since the settlement of September futures and options, called "special quotations" (SQ), late last week.
"The SQ ended on a positive tone on Friday morning, boosting investor confidence," he said. "The favourable atmosphere was brightened further by the Dow which is gaining in leaps and bounds."
Brokers said there was a fair amount of arbitrage-linked buying which was buoying the market.
Arbitrageurs simultaneously trade stocks and their underlying futures, and profit from momentary discrepancies between the prices of the two instruments.
But brokers added that Tuesday's gains were likely to be fairly limited as investors were cashing in on their purchases as soon the Nikkei climbed to take profits.
"How much the Tokyo market will rise depends on how much shopping foreign investors do," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities.
"Foreign investors turned net buyers late last week so if they continue to buy, the market may become active," Ueki said.
Orders placed by foreign investors through Japan's "Big Four" securities houses before the start of trade showed sell orders totalling 10.0 million shares against 10.5 million of buys.
"More important than rises, though, is the turnover volume," Ueki added.
"If turnover as well as cash trades increase, then that could be a signal that the Nikkei has been propelled out of the doldrums it has been mired in," Ueki said.
At midday, turnover stood at 219 million shares. In some recent sessions volume by midday has been less than half this level.
